bibl.title: Defining the healthy “core microbiome” of oral microbial communities

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A CLASS WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS DECIDED BY HOW MANY PEOPLE YOU LOOKED AT - the `core microbiome` of the healthy mouth, defined as the sequences shared by THREE unrelated volunteers across 29 intraoral sites
span.quote: There was a large overlap in the higher taxa, "species-level" phylotypes and unique sequences among the three microbiomes: 84% of the higher taxa, 75% of the OTUs and 65% of the unique sequences were present in at least two of the three microbiomes. The three individuals shared 1660 of 6315 unique sequences. These 1660 sequences (the "core microbiome") contributed 66% of the reads. The overlapping OTUs contributed to 94% of the reads, while nearly all reads (99.8%) belonged to the shared higher taxa.

span.label: how many of the oral microbiome's estimated 25,000 phylotypes are present in one mouth, and how much of that is common to unrelated healthy people
span.quote: This deep sequencing has revealed an unexpectedly high diversity of the human oral microbiome: dental plaque pooled from 98 healthy adults comprised about 10000 microbial phylotypes [ 4 ]. This is an order of magnitude higher than previously reported 700 oral microbial phylotypes as identified by cultivation or traditional cloning and sequencing [ 5 ]. Moreover, by pooling about 100 individual microbiomes and pyrosequencing these, the ecosystem still appeared undersampled: the ultimate diversity of the oral microbiome was estimated to be around 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ]. If "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects" [ 6 ], then a healthy oral microbiome should be dominated by a "core microbiome" characteristic for health. These abundant phylotypes would maintain the functional stability and homeostasis necessary for a healthy ecosystem. To date though, there is no information available on how many of the 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ] actually contribute to a single oral cavity and how common or exclusive individual oral microbiomes of unrelated healthy individuals are.

span.label: the first pyrosequencing description of whole individual oral microbiomes at site resolution, and the finding that 65% of unique sequences, 75% of OTUs and 84% of higher taxa are shared
span.quote: The major proportion of oral microbiomes was common across three unrelated healthy individuals, supporting the concept of a core-microbiome at health. The site specificity of the oral microbiome, especially between mucosal and dental sites and between saliva and dental sites, should be considered in future study designs.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The major proportion of oral microbiomes was common across three unrelated healthy individuals, supporting the concept of a core-microbiome at health. The site specificity of the oral microbiome, especially between mucosal and dental sites and between saliva and dental sites, should be considered in future study designs.

span.label: a health-defined class assembled from an intersection, in a field whose own estimates say a hundred people still undersample the ecosystem
span.quote: This deep sequencing has revealed an unexpectedly high diversity of the human oral microbiome: dental plaque pooled from 98 healthy adults comprised about 10000 microbial phylotypes [ 4 ]. This is an order of magnitude higher than previously reported 700 oral microbial phylotypes as identified by cultivation or traditional cloning and sequencing [ 5 ]. If "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects" [ 6 ], then a healthy oral microbiome should be dominated by a "core microbiome" characteristic for health. To date though, there is no information available on how many of the 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ] actually contribute to a single oral cavity and how common or exclusive individual oral microbiomes of unrelated healthy individuals are.

span.label: 454 pyrosequencing of the V5-V6 region from 29 samples across five intraoral niches in three volunteers, with sequences occurring fewer than five times discarded
span.term: 454 pyrosequencing of the V5-V6 region from 29 samples across five intraoral niches in three volunteers, with sequences occurring fewer than five times discarded
span.quote: To preclude the inclusion of sequencing artifacts or potential contaminants from sample processing, and to avoid diversity overestimation, we included only sequences occurring at least five times in further analyses. By doing so, we have also removed many less frequent but valid sequences representing the rare members of the microbiome.

span.label: **THE `CORE` IS THE INTERSECTION OF THREE PEOPLE**: `THE THREE INDIVIDUALS SHARED 1660 OF 6315 UNIQUE SEQUENCES. These 1660 sequences (THE `CORE MICROBIOME`) contributed 66% of the reads` - and the participants are `THREE HEALTHY CAUCASIAN MALE ADULTS`. **Add a fourth person and the core can only shrink.** The corpus holds classes cut from continua, classes bounded by apparatus and classes that ARE their threshold; this is the first whose extension is a function of the SAMPLE SIZE of the study that named it
span.quote: There was a large overlap in the higher taxa, "species-level" phylotypes and unique sequences among the three microbiomes: 84% of the higher taxa, 75% of the OTUs and 65% of the unique sequences were present in at least two of the three microbiomes. The three individuals shared 1660 of 6315 unique sequences. These 1660 sequences (the "core microbiome") contributed 66% of the reads. The overlapping OTUs contributed to 94% of the reads, while nearly all reads (99.8%) belonged to the shared higher taxa.

span.label: **AND ONE DATASET GIVES 66%, 93% OR 99.8% SHARED DEPENDING ON THE UNIT COUNTED**: `84% OF THE HIGHER TAXA, 75% OF THE OTUs AND 65% OF THE UNIQUE SEQUENCES were present in at least two of the three microbiomes ... THE OVERLAPPING OTUs CONTRIBUTED TO 94% OF THE READS, WHILE NEARLY ALL READS (99.8%) BELONGED TO THE SHARED HIGHER TAXA.` Same mouths, same reads, same question - and the answer moves by 34 percentage points on the choice of what to count as a thing
span.quote: There was a large overlap in the higher taxa, "species-level" phylotypes and unique sequences among the three microbiomes: 84% of the higher taxa, 75% of the OTUs and 65% of the unique sequences were present in at least two of the three microbiomes. The three individuals shared 1660 of 6315 unique sequences. These 1660 sequences (the "core microbiome") contributed 66% of the reads. The overlapping OTUs contributed to 94% of the reads, while nearly all reads (99.8%) belonged to the shared higher taxa.

span.label: **AND THE SPECIES THRESHOLD IS KEPT FOR COMPARABILITY WHILE ITS MEANING IS DENIED**: `A 3% VARIATION WITHIN A SHORT HYPERVARIABLE REGION of the SSU rRNA gene MAY NOT CORRELATE EXACTLY WITH A 3% VARIATION ALONG THE ENTIRE SSU rRNA GENE. In fact, the correlation ... MAY WELL VARY with different regions of the gene, and IN DIFFERENT CLASSES OF ORGANISMS. HOWEVER, most microbial diversity projects to date have used 3% OTUs, and TO BE CONSISTENT WITH OTHER RESEARCH ... WE HAVE CHOSEN TO USE 3% OTUs AS WELL.` The fourth `keep the suboptimal thing for continuity` in this corpus - **and the first where what is retained is a NUMBER rather than a word**
span.quote: A 97% identity in 16S rRNA gene sequences is commonly used to group "species-level" phylotypes [ 1 , 11 , 12 ]. A 3% variation within a short hypervariable region of the small subunit (SSU) rRNA gene may not correlate exactly with a 3% variation along the entire SSU rRNA gene. In fact, the correlation between genetic differences may well vary with different regions of the gene, and in different classes of organisms. However, most microbial diversity projects to date have used 3% OTUs [ 1 , 13 , 14 ], and to be consistent with other research using pyrosequencing sequences we have chosen to use 3% OTUs as well.

span.label: AND THE FILTER ADMITS IT DELETES TRUE POSITIVES: `To preclude the inclusion of sequencing artifacts or potential contaminants ... we included only sequences occurring at least five times in further analyses. BY DOING SO, WE HAVE ALSO REMOVED MANY LESS FREQUENT BUT VALID SEQUENCES REPRESENTING THE RARE MEMBERS OF THE MICROBIOME.` A published statement of what a cleaning rule costs, in the same paragraph as the rule
span.quote: To preclude the inclusion of sequencing artifacts or potential contaminants from sample processing, and to avoid diversity overestimation, we included only sequences occurring at least five times in further analyses. By doing so, we have also removed many less frequent but valid sequences representing the rare members of the microbiome.

span.label: **AND THE FILTER'S UNIT IS NOT THE CLAIM'S UNIT, WHICH LEAKS**: `Even though these sequences were found AS SINGLETONS IN A PARTICULAR MICROBIOME, THEY HAD TO BE PRESENT AT LEAST FIVE TIMES ACROSS ALL THREE MICROBIOMES according to the cut-off we applied.` **A sequence qualifies for one person's microbiome because it was abundant in the other two** - so the per-individual counts are not independent of each other, and the shared fraction is measured on data the sharing helped create
span.quote: Even though these sequences were found as singletons in a particular microbiome, they had to be present at least five times across all three microbiomes according to the cut-off we applied.

span.label: AND THE COST TO RESOLUTION IS STATED AS A NUMBER: `The stringent selection of sequences (the cut-off of 5 reads) and individual labelling and sequencing of 29 samples on a single pyrosequencing plate HAVE LARGELY REDUCED THE DEPTH OF PYROSEQUENCING RESOLUTION. On average, 10000 READS PER SAMPLE WERE OBTAINED INSTEAD OF THE 400000 READS POSSIBLE when using a full plate for a single sample. OUR FINDINGS ON DIVERSITY, THEREFORE, SHOULD BE CONSIDERED CONSERVATIVE.` A fortyfold reduction, declared
span.quote: The stringent selection of sequences (the cut-off of 5 reads) and individual labelling and sequencing of 29 samples on a single pyrosequencing plate have largely reduced the depth of pyrosequencing resolution. On average, 10000 reads per sample were obtained instead of the 400000 reads possible when using a full plate for a single sample. Our findings on diversity, therefore, should be considered conservative.

span.label: **AND `HEALTHY` IS OPERATIONALISED STRICTER THAN THE FIELD'S OWN CONVENTION, WHICH IS ITSELF A RANGE**: `THE PERIODONTAL HEALTH WAS DEFINED AS NO PERIODONTAL POCKETS DEEPER THAN 3 MM AND NO BLEEDING ON PROBING AT MORE THAN 10% OF GINGIVAL SITES ... In selecting healthy volunteers for experimental gingivitis studies, GINGIVA IS CONSIDERED HEALTHY IF BLEEDING ON MARGINAL PROBING IS PRESENT AT LESS THAN 20-25% OF GINGIVAL SITES.` The qualifier in the title rests on a bar set at half the convention, and the convention is quoted as `20-25%` rather than a number
span.quote: The periodontal health was defined as no periodontal pockets deeper than 3 mm and no bleeding on probing at more than 10% of gingival sites. The sites that were sampled did not show any bleeding. In selecting healthy volunteers for experimental gingivitis studies, gingiva is considered healthy if bleeding on marginal probing is present at less than 20-25% of gingival sites [ 24 , 25 ].

span.label: AND THE JUSTIFICATION FOR EXPECTING A CORE AT ALL IS A QUOTED APHORISM: `If `EVERYTHING IS EVERYWHERE, BUT, THE ENVIRONMENT SELECTS`, THEN A HEALTHY ORAL MICROBIOME SHOULD BE DOMINATED BY A `CORE MICROBIOME` CHARACTERISTIC FOR HEALTH. These abundant phylotypes would maintain the functional stability and homeostasis necessary for a healthy ecosystem.` The class is predicted by a century-old maxim before it is measured
span.quote: If "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects" [ 6 ], then a healthy oral microbiome should be dominated by a "core microbiome" characteristic for health. These abundant phylotypes would maintain the functional stability and homeostasis necessary for a healthy ecosystem.

span.label: AND THE FIELD'S OWN ESTIMATE SAYS A HUNDRED PEOPLE UNDERSAMPLE IT: `dental plaque pooled from 98 healthy adults comprised ABOUT 10000 MICROBIAL PHYLOTYPES. This is AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE HIGHER than previously reported 700 oral microbial phylotypes as identified by cultivation ... by pooling about 100 individual microbiomes ... THE ECOSYSTEM STILL APPEARED UNDERSAMPLED: the ultimate diversity ... was estimated to be AROUND 25000 PHYLOTYPES.` 700, then 10,000, then 25,000 - and this study has three mouths
span.quote: This deep sequencing has revealed an unexpectedly high diversity of the human oral microbiome: dental plaque pooled from 98 healthy adults comprised about 10000 microbial phylotypes [ 4 ]. This is an order of magnitude higher than previously reported 700 oral microbial phylotypes as identified by cultivation or traditional cloning and sequencing [ 5 ]. Moreover, by pooling about 100 individual microbiomes and pyrosequencing these, the ecosystem still appeared undersampled: the ultimate diversity of the oral microbiome was estimated to be around 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ]. If "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects" [ 6 ], then a healthy oral microbiome should be dominated by a "core microbiome" characteristic for health. These abundant phylotypes would maintain the functional stability and homeostasis necessary for a healthy ecosystem. To date though, there is no information available on how many of the 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ] actually contribute to a single oral cavity and how common or exclusive individual oral microbiomes of unrelated healthy individuals are.

span.label: AND WHAT IS NOT SHARED IS RENAMED RATHER THAN COUNTED: taxa `found at A VERY LOW ABUNDANCE (5-49 reads) and most likely were NOT A PART OF THE COMMENSAL ORAL FLORA, AND SHOULD BE REGARDED AS `TRANSIENTS`.` **A residual category created by the abundance filter and then given a name that explains it away** - and elsewhere the paper argues the opposite for saliva-specific sequences, whose `RELATIVELY HIGH ABUNDANCE ... SUGGESTS THAT THEY ARE A PART OF THE COMMENSAL ORAL MICROBIOTA`. Abundance decides membership in both directions
span.quote: However, these taxa were found at a very low abundance (5-49 reads) and most likely were not a part of the commensal oral flora, and should be regarded as "transients".

span.label: AND THE HABITAT'S DEFINING PROPERTY IS A PAIR OF SURFACE TYPES: `The oral cavity DIFFERS FROM ALL OTHER HUMAN MICROBIAL HABITATS BY THE SIMULTANEOUS PRESENCE OF TWO TYPES OF SURFACES for microbial colonization: SHEDDING (MUCOSA) AND SOLID SURFACES (TEETH OR DENTURES).` The site effect that follows - saliva profiles closer to mucosa than to teeth - is the reason a single `oral microbiome` is a coarser object than it sounds
span.quote: The oral cavity differs from all other human microbial habitats by the simultaneous presence of two types of surfaces for microbial colonization: shedding (mucosa) and solid surfaces (teeth or dentures). This intrinsic property of the oral cavity provides immense possibilities for a diverse range of microbiota. Once the symbiotic balance between the host and the microbiota is lost, these microbiota may become involved in disease.

span.label: AND ONE SAMPLE CAN BE BOTH THE LEAST DIVERSE AND AMONG THE RICHEST: `The two cheek samples ... showed THE LOWEST DIVERSITY among all samples. These samples were DOMINATED BY ONLY TWO OTUs EACH ... NOTABLY, THE CHEEK SAMPLE FROM S3 STILL CONTAINED ONE OF THE HIGHEST COUNTS OF TAXA (234 PHYLOTYPES), BUT OBVIOUSLY AT A VERY LOW ABUNDANCE.` Diversity by Shannon index and diversity by count disagree on the same sample - the unit problem again, one figure apart
span.quote: The two cheek samples from individual S1 and individual S3 showed the lowest diversity among all samples (Figure 6B ). These samples were dominated by only two OTUs each, identified as streptococci, with 70 sequences comprising 13% of all reads in the sample from S1, and 46 sequences comprising 17% of the reads in the cheek sample from S3. The closest match to these OTUs was Streptococcus mitis which is known to produce immunoglobulin A1 protease. This enzyme is important for the ability of bacteria to colonize mucosal membranes in the presence of S-IgA antibodies in saliva [ 22 ] and might explain high dominance of these phylotypes in these particular samples. Notably, the cheek sample from S3 still contained one of the highest counts of taxa (234 phylotypes), but obviously at a very low abundance.

span.label: THREE PEOPLE, ALL MALE, ALL CAUCASIAN, TWO FROM ONE COUNTRY: `THREE HEALTHY CAUCASIAN MALE ADULTS ... with no antibiotic use in the past three months` - and the conclusion generalises to `unrelated healthy individuals`. The exclusion list is long and precise (`no clinical signs of oral mucosal disease ... did not suffer from halitosis, did not have caries ... or periodontal disease`) and the inclusion population is three
span.quote: Three healthy Caucasian male adults (Table 1 ) with no antibiotic use in the past three months participated in the study after signed informed consent. The study was approved by the Medical Ethical Committee of the Free University Amsterdam. Each individual had a full set of natural dentition and none of them wore any removable or fixed prosthetic appliances, they had no clinical signs of oral mucosal disease and did not suffer from halitosis, did not have caries (white spot lesions of enamel or dentin lesions) or periodontal disease. The periodontal health was defined as no periodontal pockets deeper than 3 mm and no bleeding on probing at more than 10% of gingival sites. The sites that were sampled did not show any bleeding.

span.label: AND 17-19% OF EACH PERSON'S SEQUENCES ARE SHARED WITH NEITHER OTHER PERSON: `On the other hand, 17-19% OF THE UNIQUE SEQUENCES ORIGINATING FROM A SINGLE ORAL CAVITY WERE NOT SHARED WITH EITHER OF THE OTHER TWO MICROBIOMES.` The core is 66% of reads and the exclusive fraction is a fifth of sequences - both true, and only the first is in the title
span.quote: On the other hand, 17-19% of the unique sequences originating from a single oral cavity were not shared with either of the other two microbiomes (Table 3 ).

span.label: AND THE DIVERSITY FIGURES ARE AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE ABOVE THE METHODS THEY REPLACE: `each individual sample harboured 266 `SPECIES-LEVEL` PHYLOTYPES (SD 67; range 123 - 326) ... considerably higher than the previously reported 4 - 28 SPECIES PER SITE using traditional cloning and sequencing methods or 10 - 81 SPECIES using a 16S rRNA gene-based microarray.` A tenfold to fiftyfold change in a count, attributable to the instrument rather than to the mouths
span.quote: On average, each individual sample harboured 266 "species-level" phylotypes (SD 67; range 123 - 326) (Figure 6A ). This is again considerably higher than the previously reported 4 - 28 species per site using traditional cloning and sequencing methods [ 15 ] or 10 - 81 species using a 16S rRNA gene-based microarray [ 20 ].

span.label: AND THE MOTIVATING CLAIM IS THAT HEALTH IS THE UNDER-DESCRIBED STATE: `This is reflected in the AMPLE KNOWLEDGE ON THE HUMAN MICROBIOME AT THE STATE OF DISEASE AS OPPOSED TO THE LIMITED PICTURE WE HAVE OF THE HEALTHY MICROBIOME. In order to diagnose and treat disease at an early and reversible stage ONE NEEDS TO DESCRIBE THE COMMENSAL MICROBIOME ASSOCIATED WITH HEALTH.` A definition of normal proposed because the abnormal was defined first
span.quote: Usually we only become aware of their presence when the balance between the microbiota and the host is lost, and disease is manifest. This is reflected in the ample knowledge on the human microbiome at the state of disease as opposed to the limited picture we have of the healthy microbiome. In order to diagnose and treat disease at an early and reversible stage one needs to describe the commensal microbiome associated with health.

span.quote: This deep sequencing has revealed an unexpectedly high diversity of the human oral microbiome: dental plaque pooled from 98 healthy adults comprised about 10000 microbial phylotypes [ 4 ]. This is an order of magnitude higher than previously reported 700 oral microbial phylotypes as identified by cultivation or traditional cloning and sequencing [ 5 ]. Moreover, by pooling about 100 individual microbiomes and pyrosequencing these, the ecosystem still appeared undersampled: the ultimate diversity of the oral microbiome was estimated to be around 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ]. If "everything is everywhere, but, the environment selects" [ 6 ], then a healthy oral microbiome should be dominated by a "core microbiome" characteristic for health. These abundant phylotypes would maintain the functional stability and homeostasis necessary for a healthy ecosystem. To date though, there is no information available on how many of the 25000 phylotypes [ 4 ] actually contribute to a single oral cavity and how common or exclusive individual oral microbiomes of unrelated healthy individuals are.

span.quote: The two cheek samples from individual S1 and individual S3 showed the lowest diversity among all samples (Figure 6B ). These samples were dominated by only two OTUs each, identified as streptococci, with 70 sequences comprising 13% of all reads in the sample from S1, and 46 sequences comprising 17% of the reads in the cheek sample from S3. The closest match to these OTUs was Streptococcus mitis which is known to produce immunoglobulin A1 protease. This enzyme is important for the ability of bacteria to colonize mucosal membranes in the presence of S-IgA antibodies in saliva [ 22 ] and might explain high dominance of these phylotypes in these particular samples. Notably, the cheek sample from S3 still contained one of the highest counts of taxa (234 phylotypes), but obviously at a very low abundance.
